run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The app-101 payment-api application logged a burst of database connection-pool exhaustion errors on 2026-11-20: eight ERROR lines "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" from 13:46:00Z to 14:44:00Z, with wait_time_ms rising 1227 -> 4840 ms and queue_length 5-15, interleaved with successful "Payment processed successfully" lines at 13:42, 13:59 and 14:49 (b265776a-af2e-4977-abd0-27b9ee48dbd9-t1:689468e1-8673-4c6c-bfa9-543dd5f4ea58, 6d684c7f-1c3b-49d1-a77a-b7dbb2de8023-t1:952870fd-d542-4097-86eb-2c9381cba0fd). Earlier the same day the retained stream held only INFO success lines (cb15f140-224e-46bc-9a59-331bc9a61345-t0:a5d439e8-45d6-4bdd-9ce5-de5f443a7336), and a by-level count shows the level=ERROR series starting with the 13:46:40 evaluation and continuing through 14:53:35 (dea1f38b-47fa-4384-9d48-a6a69778b711-t1:ae477489-97db-4401-8150-357b12fa88ca). No pod, deployment, replicaset or service named payment-api or payment-api-101 exists in app-101 now; the namespace holds only loki (9c88112a-7c77-4c40-a478-25877f5abcc8-t0:96374813-9a9b-4274-97cf-28715a2c8a77, 2c0b7247-63aa-4465-a824-93e3df20d9e8-t0:00f50da2-2c8c-4bfd-8266-dd8e1cfb7766, 2830838e-fcc3-47ac-bbc4-eb194b7fe574-t0:2a7bdf11-4b0a-4c35-a230-ec8e9d50e515), and events show that deployment scaling 0->1 at 2026-11-21T03:56:38Z and its containers being stopped at 03:56:51Z (93759d41-da3b-426a-bf1d-f2a6d2880a39-t1:e2f15da3-77f2-4d9d-887d-0fda06ee7d2d). What exhausted the pool (slow or saturated database, demand spike, or pool sizing/leak in the app) is unresolved: every Prometheus and Jaeger query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and the database dependency is not a cluster object. The differently named otel-demo 'payment' service was checked and looked healthy in the sampled window.

claims.text: Loki lines under {namespace="app-101", job="payment-api"} carry service=payment-api, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5 and filename=/var/log/payment-api.log, and the app-101 promtail-config ConfigMap scrapes /var/log/*.log under job_name payment-api with labels job, namespace, level, service, pod.
First failure line: at 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z service payment-api logged level ERROR "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" with wait_time_ms=1227 and queue_length=10.

Exactly eight such ERROR lines appear from 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z through 2026-11-21T03:58:00Z, at 13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31 and 14:44 with wait_time_ms 1227, 2104, 1495, 2965, 4005, 4840, 2358, 3836 and queue_length 10, 11, 8, 9, 10, 8, 15, 5; the newest is 14:44:00Z, so no ERROR line appears later in the retained stream.

The same payment-api stream contains INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:42:00Z, 13:59:00Z and 14:49:00Z (payment_id PAY-5032, PAY-1800, PAY-8206), so successful payments continued while the pool-exhaustion ERROR lines were being emitted.

Earlier on 2026-11-20 the query {namespace="app-101", job="payment-api"} over 04:00:00Z-13:30:00Z returned 11 lines, all level INFO "Payment processed successfully" (12:57, 11:44, 11:40, 11:19, 06:40, 06:34, 06:00, 05:50, 05:27, 05:04, 04:24).

A Loki count_over_time by level over 2026-11-20T12:00:25Z-15:59:35Z shows the level=ERROR series with no value before the 13:46:40 evaluation and values through 14:53:35, while the level=INFO series has values from 12:57:10 onward.

The failing component is the app-101 payment-api application: the ERROR lines carry service=payment-api and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5, and cluster events show ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 creating pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5 and Deployment app-101/payment-api-101 scaling that replica set.

Events record Deployment app-101/payment-api-101 scaling replica set payment-api-101-8486559b69 from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T03:56:38Z, pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5 starting containers payment-api (python:3.9-slim) and promtail, then at 2026-11-21T03:56:51Z "Stopping container payment-api" and "Stopping container promtail"; all returned events are type Normal.

Loki holds "Payment API started" (level INFO, port 8080) from pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5 at 2026-11-21T03:56:39.366945Z, consistent with that 03:56 recreate, yet the same pod label is attached to the 2026-11-20T13:46-14:44 lines.

Namespace app-101 currently holds only the loki workload: pod loki-66445c6d6f-w22qk, Deployment loki, ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f and Service loki; no pod, deployment, replicaset or service named payment-api or payment-api-101 exists in app-101 at query time.

The event groups returned for the whole cluster inside the authorized window are 17 Normal events spanning 2026-11-21T03:56:15Z-03:56:51Z only (app-101 loki and payment-api-101 lifecycle: ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, Killing); none are dated around 2026-11-20T13:45Z and none are OOMKilled, Evicted or BackOff.

The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane was created 2026-11-20T16:31:42Z and all otel-demo pods, including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, started between 16:31Z and 16:33Z, after the 13:45Z event, so current object state cannot describe pod state at incident time.

A different entity, the otel-demo 'payment' service, was checked and looked healthy in the sampled window: Deployment payment (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, revision 1) reports 1/1 ready, ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6 was created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z, and the 60 newest filter-matching lines of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d between 2026-11-21T03:37:39Z and 03:58:02Z are "Charge request received"/"Transaction complete" with no error text.

The alerting rules in the otel-demo prometheus ConfigMap define only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio above 0.5 for 2m) plus OpsPilot self-alerts; no payment, payment-api or database-connection rule exists.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in namespace otel-demo, read at 2026-11-21T03:58:27Z, lists paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off" (paymentFailure variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off; paymentUnreachable on/off); this is the value observed after the incident and does not establish the value in effect at 2026-11-20T13:45Z.

The otel-demo flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable fault-injection flags are not a plausible cause of the app-101 payment-api errors: they belong to the otel-demo payment service (different namespace and application), both were observed off, and the app-101 error text is a database connection-pool exhaustion inside payment-api rather than a charge failure injected by a flag.

Between 2026-11-20T13:46Z and 14:44Z the payment-api application could not acquire database connections from its pool, so a subset of payment requests failed while others still succeeded; the app's own ERROR text is the only observed mechanism and no failure-rate metric was readable to size the affected fraction.

A slow or saturated database dependency is a candidate trigger of the pool exhaustion; rising wait_time_ms (1227 -> 4840) with a non-empty waiter queue (up to 15) is consistent with database-side contention, but the database is not a cluster object and its metrics and traces could not be read, so this is unverified.

An application-side pool sizing or connection-leak problem in payment-api is an alternative candidate: the pool ran out while the process kept serving some requests, and no payment-api deployment, env or config carrying pool size survived to be inspected.

A request-rate spike starting around 13:46Z could have saturated the pool; this is untested because no request-rate or latency series (for example app_payment_transactions_total or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count for payment-api) could be read in this Run.

Restore the read-only telemetry query path: the prometheus-readonly-proxy pod is Running and Ready with an endpoint, yet every Prometheus and Jaeger query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; once readable, quantify payment-api error ratio, latency and dependency latency from 13:40Z to 15:00Z on 2026-11-20.

Review the payment-api database connection pool settings (size, acquisition timeout, leak detection) alongside the database server's connection capacity and query latency for 2026-11-20T13:40-15:00Z, since the observed pattern is acquisition waiting of 1227-4840 ms with a queued wait.

Add an alert on payment-api database-connection failures, for example a Loki rule on {namespace="app-101", job="payment-api"} matching "pool exhausted", because the only loaded application alert covers checkout PlaceOrder error ratio.

Find out why Deployment app-101/payment-api-101 was scaled from 0 to 1 and then had its containers stopped within 13 seconds at 2026-11-21T03:56:38-03:56:51Z and why the deployment and pod no longer exist; change history is not integrated, so the actor and reason are unknown rather than benign.

gaps: No metric evidence: every Prometheus call (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_metric_metadata, get_label_values, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so ERROR-rate series such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code=...}, app_payment_transactions_total and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count for payment-api are unknown, not zero.

No trace evidence: every Jaeger call (traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error, parent-child call edge or dependency latency for payment-api around 2026-11-20T13:45Z was observed.

The trigger of the connection-pool exhaustion is unresolved: the database payment-api could not obtain connections to is not a Kubernetes object here and its health, latency and connection limits could not be read.

No pod-level state exists for the incident time: the payment-api deployment, replicaset and pod are absent from the current cluster, all returned events fall on 2026-11-21T03:56, and the node and every otel-demo pod were created after the incident, so restart counts, termination reasons and container status at 13:45Z are unknown.

A query for app-101 payment-api ERROR lines over 2026-11-20T03:58:07Z-13:46:00Z returned no lines (status no_data, dea1f38b-47fa-4384-9d48-a6a69778b711-t0:4f65a2ad-8120-425b-8751-b1f8d8e2ff10) and a namespace=otel-demo Loki query returned no lines for both sampled windows (7c3ae03d-5ad8-4777-a46a-78ffef7f8349-t1:d9da7255-ca16-4bff-ab85-7803b128df00, b9e1f9a2-4a03-46a5-9672-d2a7aac3f31d-t0:10079bfe-101c-4310-9737-eb4e6d783ae2, ad1285ef-91f4-4339-bf7a-3d3e9c0ac201-t0:5de338d4-703c-40ab-85e3-bc9457478f80); an empty result shows only that those queries matched nothing, so coverage of the earlier hours and of otel-demo logs is unknown.

Direct pod-log reads for otel-demo payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d over 2026-11-20T13:30-14:00Z and for prometheus-readonly-proxy returned no lines (status no_data, eeb87a2b-db19-49a4-b922-35f0fb54e5c9-t0:2f5c98ba-0d5d-495d-90bf-10b50771f4be, eeb87a2b-db19-49a4-b922-35f0fb54e5c9-t1:d7e6804f-e784-423e-a060-24ec9849b402), and a networkpolicies query returned nothing (179144e5-33e6-45fa-817d-84f16c85709e-t1:4c77d0ff-2fd3-4df4-9923-51c7ee6c9b25); absence of network policies is therefore unchecked rather than confirmed.

Provenance of the incident-time records is uncertain: the 2026-11-20T13:46-14:44 lines carry pod label payment-api-101-8486559b69-shzs5, a pod that events show being created only at 2026-11-21T03:56:38Z, so the original pod identity at incident time is unknown.

Log coverage is sparse: the retained payment-api stream holds only a handful of lines per hour, so the count of failed versus successful payments between 13:46Z and 14:44Z, and any checkout- or customer-visible impact, cannot be quantified.

Kubernetes objects and events cannot prove earlier state and the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so what (or who) changed payment-api or its database configuration before 13:46Z is unknown.
next_steps: Repair the read-only Prometheus/Jaeger access path, then quantify payment-api error ratio, p95 latency and database call latency for 2026-11-20T13:40-15:00Z.
Compare payment-api's pool configuration and the database server's connection metrics for the same window to separate pool misconfiguration or leak from a slow or saturated database.
Confirm with the service owner whether the app-101 payment-api deployment still exists (the cluster shows only its 2026-11-21T03:56 lifecycle events) and recover its pod restart/termination history.

groups:
- name: opspilot-lab

  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server

    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))

      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
